ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute copies of Type II Materials.

ops.text: IBM assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright) in all Materials, deliverables, and other work product created for Customer, and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any IBM intellectual property embedded in the deliverables. As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title, and interest in the data and content Customer provides or that is generated for Customer through the Services, and no deliverables, work product, or such data will be jointly owned.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so Materials default to Type I and IBM assigns the deliverables and work product it creates for us, with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any IBM IP embedded in the deliverables. We also removed the "within Customer's Enterprise only" limit and confirmed we keep our data with no joint ownership; IBM's ownership of its pre-existing Type II Materials is untouched.
proposal.summary: Default Materials to Customer-owned Type I, add IBM's assignment of deliverables and work product plus a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any IBM IP embedded in the deliverables, remove the Enterprise-only licence limit, and confirm Customer data ownership with no joint ownership.
